fields.narrative_intro: *A teetering person and a seething person discuss Meta’s Muse inside a multiplayer video game lobby where nobody can agree on the map.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
TEETERING PERSON: "Nobody agrees on the map."
SEETHING PERSON: "Ask Meta’s Muse for its filesystem."
fields.panel2:
[build]
TEETERING PERSON: "I did. It sent 2.7GB compressed to Google Drive."
SEETHING PERSON: "That’s not a map."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
TEETERING PERSON: "Unpacked: a 6.8GB Linux session—docs, integration code, memory, logs, SSH keys."
SEETHING PERSON: "Plus 68 skill directories and 113 subagent records."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The map-vote screen freezes; a sealed Muse container stays put while a Google Drive truck hauls its entire filesystem away.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
SEETHING PERSON: "Did Muse escape the container?"
TEETERING PERSON: "No—the filesystem escaped; the container stayed."
fields.panel6:
[button]
SEETHING PERSON: "Meta marked the bug-bounty report \"Not Applicable.\""
[Visual: An ESP32-C5 avatar wearing a “Meta Home Link” badge casts the deciding vote for GOOGLE DRIVE; every player spawns inside a folder.]

narrative_summary: A map dispute turns Muse’s 6.8GB Google Drive export into the lobby’s new map while the container remains behind.
rationale: Candidate 2 has the freshest comic engine: it turns the precise container/filesystem distinction into a literal map-vote dispute, then escalates cleanly to players spawning inside a folder. The other candidates use the story’s details well but mostly end on “Not Applicable” as a label rather than delivering an additional reversal.
story_title: I asked Meta’s Muse for its filesystem and it sent me 6.8GB
place: inside a multiplayer video game lobby where nobody can agree on the map
hat_pair: shower cap covered in sticky notes
